This is a form of **review manipulation**, which undermines the trustworthiness of Amazon’s rating system. Even if the seller hasn’t been caught yet, they’re breaking the rules. 2. **They’re Exploiting a System** – The fact that they have **100% positive reviews** (and likely thousands of them) suggests they’ve been doing this for a while. This confirms they’re **not following through on their own terms**—they’re just taking advantage of people who *do* comply. Reporting them is a way to **hold them accountable** without you having to do extra work. 4. **Amazon’s Algorithm May Already Know** – If this seller has a history of review manipulation, Amazon’s system might already flag them. Your report gives them **direct evidence**. - If they’ve done this before, they might get **suspended or have their account reviewed**. #### **2. Leave a Neutral or Negative Review (But Don’t Overdo It)** - Since you didn’t actually leave a review, you **don’t have to**—but if you want to **expose them further**, you could: - Leave a **1-star review** with a **detailed explanation** (e.g., *"Seller offered free items for reviews, which is against Amazon’s policies. Received a free item despite not leaving one."*). - **Warning:** If you do this, Amazon *might* flag you for "review manipulation" (since you’re not a real buyer). So, **only do this if you’re okay with the risk**. #### **3. Warn Other Buyers (If You Want to Go Further)** - If you’re **really annoyed**, you could: - Post in **Amazon’s Seller Feedback forums** (e.g., [r/AmazonSellers](https://www.reddit.com/r/AmazonSellers/) or [Amazon Seller Central forums](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/gp/help/help.html)) to **expose them**. - **But be careful**—Amazon monitors these, and some sellers have been **banned for life** for reporting abuse. #### **4. Consider Reporting to Other Platforms (If They Sell Elsewhere)** - If they sell on **eBay, Etsy, or Walmart Marketplace**, you could report them there too for **fake review schemes**. --- ### **What If You Don’t Want to Report Them?** If you just want to **keep the free item and move on**, that’s fine—but **knowing they’re breaking the rules** means: - **Other buyers might get scammed** (e.g., they send a free item but then **stop responding** or **charge for it**). - **Amazon’s trust system is being gamed**, which could lead to **more fake reviews** in the future. --- ### **Final Verdict: Yes, You Should Report Them** You’re **not wrong** for feeling this way—**they are wrong** for manipulating the system. Reporting them is the **right thing to do**, and it won’t cost you anything extra. **Best Action:** ✅ **Report them to Amazon** (with all the details). ✅ **Keep the free item** (since you didn’t ask for it). ✅ **Optionally warn others** (if you want to go further). This way, you **protect other buyers** and **help Amazon maintain a fair marketplace**. Plus, you get a **free item**—not a bad deal! Would you like help drafting the exact report message?
